section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Tzion" refers to the innerness of the heart, which is redeemed through Torah, while the captive powers are redeemed specifically through charity.
section.t: "Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh v'shaveha b'tzedakah"1,
and the Alter Rebbe2 explains
and the Tzemach Tzedek3
(and our Nesi'im who followed),
that Tzion refers to the aspect of the innerness of the heart.
And it is called Tzion, a term for a sign,
because the aspect of the innerness of the heart is a sign and marker for that which is above.
And in this aspect, it is impossible for there to be captivity, G-d forbid,
rather it only requires redemption,
and the redemption is through mishpat, meaning Torah,
as its Targum [translates] "according to the first judgment"4
"as the first law."
And "shaveha" (her captives) are the revealed powers of the soul that are in the aspect of enclothing in the body,
the aspect of the "leg" of the soul,
which are in a state of actual captivity,
and their redemption from captivity is specifically through tzedakah,
which is the performance of the mitzvos,
as explained elsewhere
(in the discourse "Tzion b'mishpat"5)
at length.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section presents a second interpretation that "shaveha" refers to bringing righteous ones to repentance, which is a higher level accomplished through tzedakah and specifically by Mashiach, who possesses the level of Yechidah.
section.t: Now, according to this explanation,
"Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh"
(redemption through Torah)
is higher than "shaveha b'tzedakah"
(redemption through mitzvos),
and consistent with what is explained in many places that Torah is higher than mitzvos.
However, in the Reshimot of the Tzemach Tzedek on the Prophets and Writings6,
on the verse "Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh v'shaveha b'tzedakah",
he brings an explanation,
that "shaveha" is the matter of bringing righteous ones to repentance.
For Tzion refers to the righteous7,
and the "captives" of Tzion are the matter of bringing righteous ones to repentance8,
and the redemption of the righteous is through the Torah,
but bringing righteous ones to repentance is accomplished specifically through tzedakah.
And according to this explanation, "v'shaveha b'tzedakah" is higher than "Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh",
and moreover, it is an incomparably greater elevation.
And this is also understood from the fact that bringing righteous ones to repentance is specifically through Mashiach,
as per the statement9
"Mashiach has come to bring righteous ones to repentance",
for the level of the soul of Mashiach is incomparable to the levels of other souls,
as is known in the writings of the Arizal10,
that the level of soul that the great ones of Israel merited until Mashiach is only in the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah,
and Adam HaRishon merited Chayah,
but Mashiach will merit Yechidah,
the general Yechidah of all of Israel.
And the elevation of the aspect of Yechidah over the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah is an incomparable elevation.
And this is also understood from the fact that it is called Yechidah, from the word Yachid (singular),
a term which indicates that it has no comparison to the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah.
And as is known11
the difference between Yachid and Echad,
for Echad indicates that it has a relation to another thing
[for although the term Echad is not like the term Rishon (first),
for Rishon necessitates that there is a second,
unlike Echad, for there is one and no second to it12,
nevertheless,
from the very fact that it is necessary to say "and no second", it proves that a second to it could possibly exist,
in relation to it, etc.],
but the term Yachid,
this itself indicates that there is no second to it.
And from this the magnitude of the elevation of bringing righteous ones to repentance is understood,
since this is one of the matters that will be innovated specifically by Mashiach,
the aspect of Yechidah.
